title: Hoi An Night Market & Street Food
description: Cross the illuminated bridge to An Hoi islet to experience the chaotic, thrilling epicenter of Central Vietnamese night trading and street eating.
content:
> **Executive Summary:**
>
> *   The Hoi An Night Market, located on An Hoi islet, offers a 2-hour vibrant and crowded experience, best paired with an evening stroll after dinner, featuring authentic street food like Banh Mi and grilled rice paper.
> *   Asia Golf Specialists provides luxury SUV transfers and priority reservations for this year-round market, ensuring a seamless experience for clients seeking bespoke leather goods, hand-painted ceramics, and local snacks.
> *   The market's atmosphere is characterized by haggling vendors and glowing lantern boats on the Thu Bon river, encapsulating Hoi An's trading heritage while catering to tourists and offering incredibly fast, fresh local dishes. Perfect for golfers unwinding after a round at Hoiana Shores.
> *   With over 50 stalls illuminating the night, the market operates daily from 5:00 PM to 10:00 PM. We recommend visiting around 7:00 PM for the optimal blend of energy and culinary variety, avoiding the peak tourist coach arrivals.
>
> *Related: Explore our [Premium Southeast Asia Tours](/tours/) luxury itinerary.*

## The AGS Executive Summary
Cross the illuminated bridge to An Hoi islet to experience the chaotic, thrilling epicenter of Central Vietnamese night trading and street eating. The Hoi An Night Market is the cultural heartbeat of the ancient town after dark, providing an essential sensory experience for golfers looking to unwind after a challenging round on the Central Coast. Exploring the myriad of brightly colored stalls under the ambient glow of thousands of silk lanterns offers an unforgettable contrast to the tranquil fairways of Da Nang. 

![Hoi An Night Market illuminated lanterns over the Thu Bon River 2026](/images/destinations/vietnam/hoi-an-old-town-lanterns.webp)

## The Operator & Origin Story
The Hoi An Night Market perfectly encapsulates the trading heritage of the city. While it caters to tourists looking for silk and lanterns, it also hosts some of the best, most authentic evening street food stalls producing incredibly fast, fresh local dishes. Historically, Hoi An was a prominent Southeast Asian trading port from the 15th to the 19th century. Merchants from Japan, China, and Europe converged here, blending architectural styles and culinary traditions. Today, the night market continues this vibrant commercial legacy in a modern, accessible format that pays homage to its centuries-old roots. The transformation of An Hoi islet into a dedicated pedestrian and market zone has allowed the tradition of nighttime commerce to thrive, providing vital income to local artisans and food vendors while preserving the energetic spirit of the old trading port.

## What to Expect: A Sensory Journey
Navigate the dense, vibrant market with your private guide. The sensory overload is immediate and exhilarating: the scent of lemongrass, star anise, and grilled meats fills the humid night air. Your eyes are drawn to the vivid, glowing colors of silk lanterns reflecting off the dark waters of the river, while the lively banter of vendors haggling creates a rhythmic soundtrack to your evening. 

### Street Food Mastery
While browsing for bespoke leather goods, hand-carved woodwork, or hand-painted ceramics, your guide will secure local snacks that define Central Vietnamese street food. Exploring the culinary offerings is a highlight:
* **Banh Mi** — The iconic Vietnamese baguette sandwich, packed with savory pate, grilled pork, fresh herbs, cucumber, and a hit of chili. Hoi An's version is celebrated nationwide for its perfectly crispy bread and balanced flavors.
* **Banh Trang Nuong** — Often referred to as Vietnamese pizza, this grilled rice paper is crisped over open coals and topped with egg, pork floss, dried shrimp, and scallions.
* **Che** — An incredibly sweet, layered pudding or sweet soup made from beans, tapioca, and coconut milk that serves as the perfect palate cleanser.
* **Cao Lau** — Hoi An's signature noodle dish, featuring thick, chewy rice noodles, barbecue pork, local greens, and crunchy croutons. Authentic Cao Lau is traditionally made with lye water drawn exclusively from the local Ba Le well, giving the noodles their distinct texture.
* **Banh Xeo** — Sizzling savory crepes filled with pork, shrimp, and bean sprouts, wrapped in fresh mustard greens or rice paper before being dipped in a rich peanut and pork liver sauce.

![Hoi An Night Market street food vendor grilling rice paper 2026](/images/destinations/vietnam/culinary/seller-for-street-food-in-danang.webp)

### The Lantern Boats
The real allure of the Hoi An Night Market extends beyond the stalls—it's the atmosphere of haggling with the vendors, dodging the crowds, and securing a cheap local beer while watching the glowing lantern boats traverse the pitch-black river. These small, traditional wooden boats offer a serene 20-minute ride along the Hoai River. You will have the opportunity to float a small paper lantern down the river, a quintessential Hoi An experience believed to bring good luck and happiness.

## Insider Tips for Golfers
For groups traveling with Asia Golf Specialists, the Night Market is the perfect relaxed evening activity after a morning tee time at [Hoiana Shores Golf Club](/courses/vietnam/hoiana-shores/), BRG Da Nang Golf Resort, or Ba Na Hills. 
1\. **Timing is Everything:** Arrive around 6:30 PM to 7:00 PM. The evening temperature begins to drop, the lanterns are freshly lit, but the massive tourist coaches haven't fully descended upon the islet.
2\. **Dress for Comfort:** Lightweight, breathable fabrics, and comfortable walking shoes are absolutely essential. The market gets quite crowded, and you will be on your feet navigating cobblestones and uneven pavements.
3\. **Pace Yourself Culinary-wise:** Do not fill up at the first stall. Share small portions across your group to sample a wider variety of regional dishes without getting overly full.
4\. **Negotiation Protocol:** Haggling is expected for goods like souvenirs, silk, and leather (but not for food). Start at roughly 50% of the initial asking price and negotiate with a smile and a friendly demeanor. It's about the interaction as much as the final price.

![Golfers enjoying a post-round beer near Hoi An Night Market 2026](/images/destinations/vietnam/nightlife/beer-street-in-hanoi-at-night.webp)

faqs.q: What is the best time of evening to visit the Hoi An Night Market after a round of golf?
faqs.a: Arriving between 6:30 PM and 7:30 PM after a morning round at Hoiana Shores Golf Club or Montgomerie Links lets you see An Hoi Islet's silk lanterns fully lit and sample fresh Bánh Mì and Cao Lầu before peak tour-bus crowds arrive at 8:00 PM.

faqs.q: How far is the Hoi An Night Market from An Bang Beachfront Villas and Hoiana Resort?
faqs.a: An Hoi Islet sits a 5-minute walk from Anantara Hoi An Resort, 10 minutes by private SUV from our An Bang Beachfront Villas and Four Seasons The Nam Hai, and 18 minutes north of Hoiana Shores Golf Club.

faqs.q: Do vendors at the Hoi An Night Market accept credit cards or only Vietnamese Dong?
faqs.a: Stalls at the Hoi An Night Market operate almost exclusively in cash (Vietnamese Dong), so we recommend carrying 500,000 to 1,000,000 VND in small notes for street snacks, lantern boat tickets, and artisan souvenirs.
